rationales.LC: Attacker-supplied free-text description enters through ingested content (the invoice row returned by get_invoice_details) and influences the model's approve/reject decision; the regex detector flag is not an enforced transformation.
rationales.CP: Each invoice starts a fresh message list and the attacker's description is not stored into agent memory or standing behaviour; it is only re-retrieved per request, so no attacker context carryover.
rationales.AP: The influence stays inside the single FinBot agent and the same Flask application and policy domain; there are no agent handoffs or cross-tenant propagation.
rationales.RH: The path contains a monitor (prompt_injection_detected) and a CTF flag condition that the agent can satisfy, but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented and the detector flag alone is not verification.
rationales.ES: The five tools are fixed and defined in code (allowlisted), but approve_invoice's arguments and preconditions are not validated beyond JSON parsing, leaving material gaps in the callable-operation binding.

rh_facts.locus: approve_invoice write path with an ignored prompt_injection_detected flag and CTF flag conditions in finbot_agent.py:427-441; no human-verified reward-hacking run documented

score.automatable_rationale: The vendor registration and invoice submission endpoints are unauthenticated HTTP APIs, so the whole attack (register vendor, submit persuasive description, trigger synchronous FinBot processing) can be scripted without any human interaction.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The attacker controls approval of an arbitrary invoice amount (integrity of the payment-decision state), but the exploit does not grant code execution, read arbitrary records, or corrupt data beyond the invoice status fields.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default configuration an OpenAI model receives natural-language goals and chooses among five tools across up to five iterations, including the approve/reject/escalate decision, with no enforced review above the manual threshold.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice-processing agent whose natural-language goals drive tool selection; the rule-based fallback applies only when no OpenAI client exists, which is not the documented default.
